description: Makes a spreadsheet in a connected Google account, named by id: its title, one tab, the header columns (with a type each, text by default) and, optionally, one example row. It lands in the account’s own Google Drive and answers with its id, link, tabs and columns, which an automation’s sheet steps then use. Sends nothing to anyone.

columns.description: The header row, first column first: 26 at most, A to Z.

name.description: The column’s header, as the first row shows it and as Find a row matches it (any case).

type.description: What the column holds. text, the default: the example row’s cell is formatted as text, so what the owner types over it stays exactly as typed (a phone number, a code). number or date: that cell is not formatted as text, so what the owner types over it is read the way Google Sheets reads anything typed. The example value itself is written as text either way. With no example row it changes nothing in the sheet.

example_row.description: One row under the header for the owner to type over, as wide as `columns`. Absent: the sheet has the header row only.

id.description: The id in the resource path.

title.description: The spreadsheet’s name, in the owner’s words.

name: create_spreadsheet
title: Make a spreadsheet
